searchText: testing bridge <dannyryan> ‌‎ ‎ 👍 We just set up a new discord channel for the EthGlobal Scaling hackathon project we are starting: <#826479341784662056> ☀️ Get involved if you want to experiment with Merge testnets, and maybe contribute to a combined sharding prototype! There is a new doc giving an overview of the consensus upgrade from Mainnet perspective. The doc is in active development and it would be great to get more eyes on it. Discussion will happen during the Merge Implementers call 1. Looking forward to your questions and comments, https://hackmd.io/@n0ble/ethereum_consensus_upgrade_mainnet_perspective <vbuterin> Added some comments <vbuterin> Hmm, I do think that we need to think much more carefully and explicitly about the transition *process* (ie. the first embedded block) <vbuterin> That's the biggest potential source of landmines imo <vbuterin> One possible landmine is the beacon chain reorging from a chain that has embedded application blocks to a chain that does not <vbuterin> That is why in my original proposal I took care to make the fork choice rule stateless <vbuterin> so it could swing back and forth between following the beacon chain and following max tot diff if needed <vbuterin> Whereas this doc seems to take "one way switch" route, which seems dangerous? <vbuterin> Or am I missing something? <vbuterin> Also, what are the requirements for what the first embedded block must point to as a parent? <vbuterin> (ie. the transition conditions) <vbuterin> I'm definitely happy with the new block format proposal! <vbuterin> And that thinking is being done on the sync process! <n0ble> One way switch doesn’t prevent re-orgs with changing of the last PoW block. If the first PoS block is orphaned the other one could be produced even with the different PoW block as a parent, then the application-layer will re-org to the latter one if it’s considered as valid and so force until network start making progress (re @vbuterin: Whereas this doc seems to take "one way switch" route, which seems dangerous?) <n0ble> Are you referring to the transition conditions, i.e. total difficulty? If yes, then this is just not specified in the doc because this is the consensus-layer responsibility. Though, I thing we should add this for clarity (re @vbuterin: Also, what are the requirements for what the first embedded block must point to as a parent?) <n0ble> definitely agree, need more details and potential edge cases to think through and document out (re @vbuterin: Hmm, I do think that we need to think much more carefully and explicitly about the transition *process* (ie. the first embedded block)) <dankrad> > [Mainnet perspective] this is confusing. the beacon chain IS mainnet <dankrad> application chain perspective? <n0ble> Application-layer perspective, probably <n0ble> sorry, about to go afk now, will address the comments and questions tomorrow <vbuterin> > If the first PoS block is orphaned the other one could be produced even with the different PoW block as a parent, then the application-layer will re-org to the latter one if it’s considered as valid and so force until network start making progress <vbuterin> hmm I see <vbuterin> so it could cause fork choice divergence for as long as there are no honest proposers <vbuterin> (eg. if many proposers in a row after the merge are all dishonest, then nodes that saw the PoS chain that gets orphaned before it got orphaned will be stuck on that chain, but nodes that did not will stay on the PoW chain, at least until the next honest proposer comes along) <vbuterin> maybe this isn't that bad and I should just accept it <vbuterin> Aaah I see (re @n0ble: Are you referring to the transition conditions, i.e. total difficulty? If yes, then this is just not specified in the doc because this is the consensus-layer responsibility. Though, I thing we should add this for clarity)
